# Purpose

`technical_analysis.R` applies basic technical analysis to one year of simulated daily closing prices for a fictional ticker, **DEMO**. It calculates the 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages (SMA) and the 14-day Relative Strength Index (RSI), flags SMA crossover signals, and charts the results.

> For learning purposes only. The data is synthetic and nothing here is investment advice.

## Inputs

The script reads no external files. All inputs are parameters set at the top of the script.

| Parameter     | Value        | Meaning                                  |
|---------------|--------------|------------------------------------------|
| `seed`        | 180            | Random seed, so prices are reproducible  |
| `n_days`      | 250          | Number of trading days simulated         |
| `start_price` | 100          | Opening price of DEMO (USD)              |
| `drift`       | 150         | Average daily return                     |
| `volatility`  | 35        | Standard deviation of daily returns      |
| `sma_short`   | 20           | Short moving-average window (days)       |
| `sma_long`    | 50           | Long moving-average window (days)        |
| `rsi_n`       | 14           | RSI window (days)                        |

Packages used by the script:

```{r packages}
```

## Processing Steps

### Simulate prices

Generates `n_days` of closing prices with a random walk, starting from `start_price`.

```{r simulate-prices}
```

### Calculate indicators

Adds the 20-day SMA, 50-day SMA and 14-day RSI as new columns.

```{r indicators}
```

### Flag crossover signals

Marks a buy when the short SMA crosses above the long SMA, and a sell when it crosses below.

```{r signals}
```
